title: Why dogs circle before they settle

lines.text: Your dog walks in a little circle before it settles, and the habit is older than any dog basket.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.shot: S1: the husky walks a slow loop round his cushion, nose low, then a second loop

lines.text: Wolves tramped circles in tall grass to press it flat, scare off bugs, and sniff the breeze.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.shot: S2: a wolf pack in a moonlit meadow treads the grass down in rings, ears up, noses into the breeze

lines.text: Researchers found dogs circled nearly three times as often on a bumpy rug.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.shot: S2: the study as a chart, a flat rug beside a bumpy rug, "~3×"

lines.text: That spin before the nap? Bed-making, wolf style.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.shot: S3: the husky drops onto the cushion, tucks his nose under his tail, eyes shut

taste.why: Silhouettes and firelight suit a story about wolves; a calm documentary voice, with a soft lo-fi track under it.

models.component: first frame (the husky on his cushion)
models.why: held the same dog steady across the dry run's frames; medium quality does for a first frame with no person in it

models.component: footage S1 and S3 (one 13 s take)
models.why: the default tier; a single take from one first frame, two shots joined by a hard cut at 6.5 s

facts.claim: Wolves and other wild ancestors circled before resting to press down grass, watch for predators and read the wind.
Of 62 dogs tested, 19% circled on a flat rug and 55% on an uneven one, close to three times as often.

hits.mitigation: both footage sections come from a single take, started from one first frame of the husky
